US._sources: Web search 2026-09-11 (NewsNation, Wikipedia, Business Standard, Al Jazeera, Modern Diplomacy). Weights are Claude's own judgment translating reported troop counts/base function into a 0-1 scale -- not an official metric, no such thing exists publicly. Adjust freely.

_notes.Qatar: Al Udeid AB, ~10,000 troops, forward HQ for USAFCENT/CENTCOM air ops -- largest single US installation in the region
_notes.Kuwait: Ali Al-Salem AB + Camps Arifjan/Buehring, ~13,500 troops -- largest US troop count in the region, main logistics/command hub
_notes.Bahrain: Naval Support Activity Bahrain, ~8,300-9,000 personnel, 5th Fleet HQ -- reported rendered inoperable by Iranian strikes during the 2026 war
_notes.Iraq: Ain Al Asad AB, Erbil AB -- significant but politically sensitive/less 'permanent' given Iraqi sovereignty constraints
_notes.UAE: Al Dhafra AB (USAF/drone ops hub), Jebel Ali Port (US Navy's largest regional port of call)
_notes.Saudi Arabia: Prince Sultan AB, ~2,300 personnel, Patriot air-defense focus -- smaller footprint than Qatar/Kuwait/Bahrain
_notes.Jordan: Part of the network per CFR/Al Jazeera's 8-permanent-presence list; less base-specific public detail than the top 3, but real strategic relevance (Iran has targeted it repeatedly in 2026)
_notes.Oman: Airfield access under defense arrangements for logistics/contingency support -- access, not a major standing base
_notes.Egypt: On the 8-permanent-presence list; minimal combat/basing detail publicly reported -- mostly logistics/access
_notes.Syria: Explicitly reported as uncertain/reduced as of early 2026 -- treat as time-sensitive, re-check before trusting this weight
